evidence: src/application/AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts: `validateExecute(status: unknown): void { if (!isOrderStatus(status)) throw new DomainError("invalid", "Unknown order state"); }` is never called by execute(orderId: string)
src/application/ListOrdersByStatusUseCase.ts: `execute(status: unknown)` begins with the same check: `if (!isOrderStatus(status)) throw new DomainError("invalid", "Unknown order state");`
src/application/AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts and src/application/CancelOrderUseCase.ts both contain `if (!order) throw new DomainError("not_found", `Order ${orderId} not found`)`
src/application/dto.ts: toOrderDto/toStockLevelDto are used consistently by all use cases, so the DTO mapping is used correctly everywhere
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module covers one concern: order and stock use cases plus their DTOs, all mapped through dto.ts (toOrderDto, toStockLevelDto). It breaks the rubric in one place. AdvanceOrderUseCase has a public method, validateExecute(status: unknown), that repeats the status check in ListOrdersByStatusUseCase.execute word for word: `if (!isOrderStatus(status)) throw new DomainError("invalid", "Unknown order state")`. That is the same rule written twice. It also doesn't belong in AdvanceOrderUseCase. That use case's execute takes an orderId, never a status, and it never calls validateExecute. So the check is a stray copy of another use case's input validation. The same rule now has two homes, and changing it in one file can leave the other out of date. A smaller duplication also exists: the find-or-throw "not_found" check appears in both AdvanceOrderUseCase and CancelOrderUseCase. This pattern is common in use-case code, so it isn't the main reason for the failure.

violations.message: validateExecute(status: unknown) copies the order-status check and the 'Unknown order state' error from ListOrdersByStatusUseCase.execute. Advancing an order never uses a status, and execute never calls this method, so the rule now lives in two places.
